config.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year

personas.name: Margaret
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to finish her term without a fuss

personas.name: Tunde
personas.goals: Accurate books and a healthy reserve
personas.hidden_agenda: Training a successor and wants the process documented

personas.name: Ines
personas.goals: Classroom grants that actually cover supplies
personas.hidden_agenda: The library is her real priority

personas.name: Craig
personas.role: Parent volunteer, runs the book fair
personas.goals: A bigger book fair next year
personas.hidden_agenda: Remembers the good parts of every event

agenda.title: Grants and requests
agenda.goal: Set the classroom grants and decide on the library and assembly requests

agenda.title: Timeline
agenda.goal: Agree the steps to the membership vote

beats.summary: Last year's numbers; Craig's book fair memory is generous
Next year's fundraisers; a quick detour about the new caretaker's dog
Classroom grants and two requests; the teacher count nobody checks
Steps to the vote; one question left open

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's start with last year, then work forward. Tunde, could you give us the summary?

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Of course. Income was twenty-two thousand seven hundred, and we spent twenty-one thousand one hundred and fifty.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: So a small surplus.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Yes. The reserve is now six thousand four hundred.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: And the book fair did well, didn't it? I think it made about four thousand.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: It made two thousand nine hundred and fifty. Sales were close to four thousand, but that's before the publisher's share.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: Ah, that's right. The publisher takes their cut.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: It's still the best fundraiser we have.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: And movie night?

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Six hundred and forty. Small, but the families enjoy it.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: The popcorn machine nearly caught fire, if I remember correctly.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: The popcorn machine is fine now. The caretaker replaced the element.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: How many families are members at the moment?

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Fifty-eight percent of families. Up a little from last year.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: That's good for a school our size.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Income for next year. I'd suggest we keep what works.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: The book fair, certainly. I'd like to try two book fairs, one in autumn and one in spring.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Would the publisher agree to two in one year?

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: They offer it to every school. We've just never asked.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Two book fairs would mean more volunteers.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: I'll ask the publisher about a spring date and check how many volunteers they recommend.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Does the publisher pay for delivery, or do we?

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Thank you, Craig. And movie night stays.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Movie night stays. It's low effort.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Has everyone met Pepper? The caretaker brings her in on Fridays now.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: The children adore her. She sat through a whole assembly last week.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Shall we add a sponsored walk? Other schools do very well with them.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: It would need a permit for the park, I think.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: The children would enjoy it, and it gets families outside.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Let's think about the walk over the summer and decide in September.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: That seems sensible.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Grants. The classroom grant is a hundred and fifty per teacher at the moment.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Which is not much. A box of good markers costs a fortune.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: With eighteen teachers, that's two thousand seven hundred.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Could we raise it to two hundred?

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: That would make a real difference to the younger classes.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Then the classroom grant goes up to two hundred per teacher. We can afford it.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Thank you. And the library request. Three thousand, for new books and two reading chairs.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: Three thousand is more than the book fair makes.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: The library hasn't had new chairs since before I started here.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: It would be lovely if somebody looked into the council's library grants.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: The reserve could cover part of it. Perhaps half from the reserve and half from next year's income.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: I like that. It doesn't touch the classroom grants. And the science assembly? The company quoted twelve hundred.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: The children talked about last year's for weeks. The exploding pumpkin.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: Twelve hundred for one morning is a lot, though.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: It's two hundred and sixty-eight children for one morning. That's under five dollars each.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Then the library gets its three thousand, half from the reserve, and the assembly stays.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: I'll update the draft budget with those changes this week.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: Timeline. The vote is on June third.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: The draft should go to families two weeks before, so around the twentieth of May.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Could it be shared in the school newsletter as well? More people read that than the emails.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: That's a good idea. The newsletter goes out every other Friday.

turns.speaker: Craig
turns.text: I'll write a short piece about the book fairs for the same newsletter.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Should we explain why the reserve is going down? Some families watch it closely.

turns.speaker: Ines
turns.text: Who prints the voting slips this year? Last year we ran short.

turns.speaker: Margaret
turns.text: The school office has offered. I'll confirm with them. That's everything. Thank you all, and good night.

turns.speaker: Tunde
turns.text: Good night.
